title: Bootcamp mentor rotation — sprint checklist and mentor guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a working checklist and quick-reference guide for the Bootcamp Mentor Rotation. It's intended for People Ops and the volunteer mentor pool who run 2-week mentor sprints for newly hired ICs. Focus: reduce cognitive overhead for mentors, standardize critical early experiences, capture handoffs, and provide lightweight evaluation notes for hiring managers.

Scope and intent: 
- Applies to all full-time IC hires in engineering (new grad and experienced) who enter the 2-week bootcamp.
- Not the full 90-day plan — this is the first two-week mentor-run sprint that sits before manager-driven 30/60 plans.
- Goal: ensure new hire can ship a tiny, meaningful change, knows where to find infra, and has a concrete mentor contact for first 30 days.

High-level cadence: 
- Mentor rotation length: 2 weeks per mentor cohort. Each cohort supports 3–6 new hires depending on load.
- Mentor shifts: mentor on-call for the cohort Mon–Fri, 9am–5pm local time; one async owner for evenings/weekend follow-ups.
- Weekly sync: Thursday 30m retrospective with People Ops + mentors to capture blockers and adjust next cohort.

Before week 0 (prep checklist for People Ops):
- Assign mentor cohort and confirm availability in calendar. (Owner: People Ops)
metadata: (internal) make sure mentor list matches roster in People Ops sheet
content_continued:
Mentor onboarding (1 day before cohort starts):
- Quick 45m run-through with People Ops: goals, escalation path, and repo access list.
- Share cohort-specific Slack channel and add all participants. Template message pinned in channel (see templates below).

Day-by-day mentor checklist (week 1):
Day 0 (pre-boarding):
- Confirm new hires have accounts + hardware status (ask IT if any delays).
- Send welcome template with first-day agenda and GitHub org access steps.

Day 1: orientation + small wins
- 9:00 AM: group welcome (30m) — intros, goals for sprint, who to ping.
- 10:00 AM: dev environment setup pairing (mentor pairs 1:1 until green build).
- 3:00 PM: assign first micro-task (tiny README fix, docs update, or test that exercises CI).
- End of day: 15m check-in: any blockers?

Days 2–3: shadowing + first change
- Pair on first change; mentor reviews PR checklist aloud.
- Teach repo navigation (where CI config lives, where infra tickets are filed).
- Encourage small non-blocking PR by end of day 3.

Day 4: ramping independence
- New hire owns a small bug or doc improvement; mentor reviews with lightweight rubric (see below).
- Introduce tracing/debugging workflow and common flakiness notes.

Day 5: demo + weekly retro
- 20m demo: new hire shows what shipped; celebrate.
- 30m cohort retro: wins, blockers, action items for People Ops.

Week 2: ownership + context depth
- Focus on cross-team touchpoints (console, infra, SRE).
- Assign a slightly larger scoped ticket (2–3 days).
- Mid-week: manager intro + handoff meeting to align 30/60/90 expectations.
- End of sprint: final showcase and short written intake for manager.

Mentor responsibilities (summary):
- Be primary human contact for cohort during working hours.
- Ensure green build + first merge for each new hire.
- Surface political/contextual knowledge (who owns the schema, who to call about infra).
- Flag performance/fit signals early (use evaluation rubric below).
- Add structured notes to the Handoff form and upload to People Ops doc.

Handoff form (one-line items mentors must fill at end of sprint):
- New hire name 
- Completed tasks (links to PRs)
- Remaining blockers (short)
- Suggested 30/60 goals (3 bullets)
- Confidence level: High / Medium / Low (mentor judgement)
- Anything urgent manager should know

Quick evaluation rubric (for first two weeks) — use simple signals, not hiring decisions:
- Technical: completed at least one merged PR that changed behavior (Yes/No).
- Autonomy: required prompting to complete task (None/Some/High).
- Communication: responded to async requests and asked clarifying questions (Good/Okay/Needs coaching).
- Learning velocity: picked up codebase concepts after 3 pair sessions (High/Medium/Low).
- Cultural fit markers: collaborated respectfully, attended team events (Yes/No).

Slack + email templates (paste into shared channel):
- Welcome DM (to new hire): "Hi {name}, welcome! I'm {mentor}. Today we'll get your dev env green and land a small PR. Ping me in #{cohort-channel} or DM for fast help."
- Weekly retro invite: short agenda — demos, blockers, ops actions.

Handoff calendar template: 30m meeting — participants: new hire, mentor, hiring manager, People Ops lead. Agenda: status, PRs, blockers, 30/60 outcomes.

Escalation path:
- Tier 1: Mentor (first line)
- Tier 2: People Ops lead (if access / policy issue)
- Tier 3: Hiring manager + Eng SRE (if infra or production blocker)

Recordkeeping and artifacts:
- Store all mentor handoff forms in People Ops folder: Confluence link referenced above.
- Tag PRs with "bootcamp-first-merge" label for metrics.
- People Ops will compile a weekly dashboard of merge rates and env failures.

Measurement / success indicators:
- Target: 90% of new hires merge at least one PR in first 10 working days.
- Target: average time-to-green dev env < 2 days.
- Qualitative: manager satisfaction survey at day 14 > 4/5.

Open questions / TODOs (working list):
- Determine mentor compensation/recognition (rotation stipend vs. kudos) — @Maeve to draft proposal.
- Should we gate cohort size by mentor seniority? Experiment with 3 vs. 6 hires.
- Automate calendar invites and handoff form creation via HR system (Jira ticket referenced).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a 15m 'mentor office hours' drop-in each morning in addition to pairing blocks.
- Lightweight mentor checklist card in Monday.com for visibility.
- Keep rubric intentionally coarse — avoid premature hiring judgments.

Document history: initial draft 2025-08-18 by Aisha. Updated 2025-09-02 with templates and rubric after pilot cohort 5.

If you're a mentor reading this: copy the DM template, add your calendar blocks, and please paste completed handoffs as a single comment in Confluence-ONBOARD-1234. Thanks — Aisha
